chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alawi from al-Amriki from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother Musa (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the boy, when does fasting and prayer become obligatory upon him? He said: "When he approaches puberty and knows fasting and prayer."

Regarding the boy, when does prayer become obligatory upon him? He said: "When thirteen years have passed for him; if he experiences wet dream before that, then prayer has become obligatory upon him and the pen has been lifted [or recorded] for him. And the girl is the same; if thirteen years have passed for her or she menstruates before that, then prayer has become obligatory upon her and the pen has been recorded for her."

key_terms.جَرَى الْقَلَمُ: the pen was recorded (deeds are counted)

ai.seo_question: At what age do fasting and prayer become obligatory for boys and girls in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim clarifies the criteria for *bulugh* (puberty) by linking physical signs—wet dreams for boys and menstruation for girls—to the onset of religious obligation (*taklif*) and the 'lifting of the pen' from children. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that while age thirteen is the default threshold, the actual biological markers can trigger accountability earlier, ensuring that the recording of deeds begins precisely when the child gains sufficient understanding and physical maturity.
